steps.title: P4c-3 falls look
steps.intro: Produced by tools/render_jobs/jobs/falls_look.json at 1920x1080. A new 150 ft temperate forest map (seed 1234): a two-tier Tier step (Sculpt's Tier twice) with a straight waist river drawn from its top toward the camera along the grid, and a 13 m Raise hill east of it (an 8 m dome, its flank at 44 degrees at the steepest, a steep run of about 9 m; it stands clear of the river in screen space, since a hill between the camera and a stroke's path catches the pointer's ray) with an ankle stream drawn from its top down the flank toward the camera about 22 degrees off the grid (the angle where a grid-sampled crease saws), so P4c-1 plans two hillside falls; then a second waist river carved through the editor API (probes/water.gd carve, no pointer) from the step's top off its far edge, falling away from the camera. The carved ground is captured with the water hidden at home and at zoom 8 on each fall's foot (probes/falls.gd names them); then with the water shown at zoom 8 on every fall. Judge the ground: the rock lip, the face, the notch's side walls (P4c-2b: a channel width or two of rock, not a quarry), the plunge bowl, any sawtooth or hanging upper water. Judge the water (P4c-3, placeholder material): the curtain hangs from the lip to the pool without cutting into the rock, no draped sheet, no flat lip quad over the face, the foam ring on the pool, the mist facing the camera inside the notch.
